recentItems.title: What a Magnitude 7.0 Earthquake Would Do to New York (S2, E8) | Mega Disasters | Full Episode
recentItems.description:
What would happen if a massive earthquake struck the heart of New York City?

Most people associate earthquakes with the West Coast, but NYC sits on a complex network of ancient fault lines that pose a significant seismic risk. In this full episode of Mega Disasters, we investigate the terrifying reality of a "Big One" hitting Manhattan. From the 125th Street Fault to the science of soil liquefaction, discover why the city’s iconic skyscrapers and historic brownstones might be more vulnerable than you think.

In this episode, we explore:

-Historical Precedent: Looking back at the 1884 New York earthquake and the 1944 Massena disaster.

-The 125th Street Fault: Understanding the geological "ticking time bomb" running right through Harlem.

-Liquefaction Danger: Why landfill areas like Battery Park City could turn into sinking mud during a quake.

-Engineering vs. Nature: How the Empire State Building and modern skyscrapers are designed to survive—and where the infrastructure might fail.

The Aftermath: A minute-by-minute simulation of a 6.5 magnitude quake and the $250 billion destruction it would leave behind.

recentItems.title: The High-Tech World of Ancient China (S1, E10) | Ancient Discoveries | Full Episode
recentItems.description:
Discover the mind-blowing technology of the ancient world in this full episode of Ancient Discoveries.

While Europe was in the Dark Ages, Ancient China was a global technological superpower. From precision earthquake detectors to massive industrial factories, see how these ancient inventors were over a thousand years ahead of their time. Was our modern industrial revolution actually a "reinvention" of ancient Chinese engineering?

In this episode, we explore:

-The World's First Seismograph: How Chang Hang’s 2nd-century invention predicted earthquakes 1,600 years before the West.

-Deep Drilling Technology: The 2,000-year-old "Heaven Carts" used to reach natural gas and oil.

-Mass Production & Heavy Industry: The Song Dynasty’s massive iron-forging blast furnaces and automated factories.

-The Cosmic Engine: Su Song's 11th-century astronomical computer—the most complex machine of the Middle Ages.


#AncientChina #Engineering #HistoryChannel #AncientDiscoveries #IndustrialRevolution #FullEpisode

recentItems.title: The Radium Girls: The Job That Was Killing Them | HISTORY This Week
recentItems.description:
September 2, 1922. Twenty-four-year-old Mollie Maggia has a toothache. In less than a year, this otherwise healthy young woman will be dead. Others like her will soon follow. They’d all shared what seemed to be a dream job: applying glow-in-the-dark paint to clock faces. The paint glowed because it was saturated with radium, the wonder element of its day. And now that radium has burrowed inside the bones and lungs of the women. How did a supposed wonder element and cure-all come to be seen for what it was – a deadly poison? And how did a group of courageous young women, racing the clock of their own mortality, expose this truth?

Special thanks to Kate Moore, author of The Radium Girls: The Dark Story of America’s Shining Women. Also, a huge thank you to Art Fryer, nephew of Grace Fryer, one of the “Radium Girls.”

**This episode originally aired September 12, 2022.

recentItems.title: The Doctor Who Outwitted Typhoid Mary | History Honors 250
recentItems.description:
Sara Josephine Baker was a pioneer of public health programs min the early 1900s. Baker was the first woman to head NYC’s new Bureau of Child Hygiene in 1908 and pioneered many medical advancements for children health at a time when dysentery, smallpox, and typhoid were common killers. And Baker played a crucial role in tracking down Mary Mallon, otherwise known as Typhoid Mary, who infected as many as 122 people with the disease. Baker worked with police to track down a Mallon who even tried to violently attack Baker when they attempted to bring her into a hospital by police custody. Baker’s later work would help start the Federal Children’s Bureau and Public Health Services (now the Department of Health and Human Services.)

America The Story of Us is an epic 12-hour television event that tells the extraordinary story of how America was invented. With highly realistic CGI animation, dramatic recreations and thoughtful insights from some of America’s most respected artists, business leaders, academics and intellectuals, it is the first television event in nearly 40 years to present a comprehensive telling of America’s history. Elaborate, ambitious and cinematic, America The Story of Us will take you into the moments when Americans harnessed technology to advance human progress, from the rigors of linking the continent by transcontinental railroad–the internet of its day–to triumphing over vertical space through the construction of steel structured buildings to putting a man on the moon. It is an intensive look at the people, places and things that have shaped our nation, and the tough and thrilling adventure that is America’s 400-year history.
